title: Hierarchical model arbitrator for fast decode paths and rollback procedures
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a hierarchical arbitration layer that selects a fast-path decode model/router using kernel fingerprints, temporal workload signals, and a per-tenant acceptance budget. The arbitrator should enable low-latency optimistic decodes while guaranteeing graceful, measurable rollback to the safe decoder when acceptance signals indicate degradation.

Scope and constraints:
- Make minimal runtime changes to scheduling and kernel selection code paths to reduce integration risk.
- Support multi-model stacks (e.g., small quantized model -> medium quantized -> full fp16) and heterogeneous hardware pools.
- Keep per-token tail latency SLOs and cost impact visible through Console.

Design overview:
1) Hierarchical arbitrator: a compact decision graph with three ordinal tiers: Fast (aggressive kernels/quantized small models), Stable (medium models with conservative kernels), Safe (full model fallback). The arbitrator scores each request by a composite score: kernel_fingerprint_score + workload_signal_score + tenant_budget_score + prefix_confidence_hint.
2) Kernel fingerprint sampling: lightweight sampler attached to the prefill stage that computes a per-request fingerprint (token length, attention pattern indicator, kv-peak estimate). Fingerprints are hashed into buckets that map to learned kernel suitability statistics.
3) Temporal acceptance decay: acceptance threshold decays for a tenant after a sequence of failures to avoid thrashing. A grace window gives the arbitrator the ability to continue fast-paths for a short burst while telemetry stabilizes.
4) Rollback credit system: successful fast-path decodes accrue credit; failures consume it. Credits gate whether a tenant can be routed to the fast tier. Credits decay over time to adapt to workload changes.
5) Staged fallback policy: immediate kernel fallback (within decode) for micro-issues, and full model fallback (reroute to Stable/Safe) when cumulative acceptance falls below thresholds.
6) Shadowing and offline replay: shadow most judgements for 2 weeks to gather acceptance labels before full rollout. Use offline replay simulator with live kernel latency profiles to estimate cost and latency gains.

Instrumentation and metrics required:
- prefill_accept_rate (per model tier, per tenant)
- first_token_latency and steady_state_token_latency (p50/p95/p99)
- kernel_mismatch_rate (cases where kernel choice increased latency or memory)
- rollback_rate and rollback_latency_penalty
- budget_consumption and credit_balance
- cost_delta_per_1k_tokens (estimated)

Acceptance criteria:
- Fast-path increases median token throughput for 80% of observed short-context requests without raising p99 token latency > 5% from baseline Safe path under controlled load tests.
- Rollback_rate < 2% for tenant cohorts in pilot after two-week shadowing.
- Observability: Console shows per-tenant fast-path utilization, credit balances, and rollback events with links to example traces.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Overfitting to kernel fingerprints for narrow workloads could increase failures on bursty or adversarial inputs. Mitigation: conservative defaults, strong shadowing, and decayable credits.
- Increased telemetry costs from shadowing and sampling. Mitigation: adaptive sampling and aggregated histograms.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: implement fingerprint sampler and lightweight arbitrator API (shadow-only). Create simulator to replay historical traffic and compute acceptance labels.
- Week 2: integrate kernel suitability store and credit ledger. Start closed-canary (internal tenants).
- Week 3: expose telemetry and Console widgets; add rollout toggles for tenant cohorts.
- Week 4-5: external pilot with 3 customers, iterate thresholds.

Rollout knobs:
- global fast_path_enabled boolean
- per-tenant credit_threshold and grace_window_ms
- sampled_shadow_rate
- acceptance_thresholds per model tier

- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Hierarchical+Arbitrator+Design+v1

- Prepare a short demo for platform owners showing Console widgets and rollback traces.
updates: 2026-03-01: Spike completed for fingerprint sampler. Early samplers add ~0.2ms per prefill on p4. Collected 48M fingerprints from last 7 days (sampling=1%).

2026-03-03: Simulator prototype can replay prefixes and score acceptance with live kernel latencies. Initial sim shows 18% median token cost reduction for short prompts using Fast tier on CPU-backed quantized models.
2026-03-06: Reworked credit decay parameters after internal review — increased decay half-life from 10m to 60m to reduce oscillations for bursty tenants.
2026-03-08: PR #3872 opened for arbitrator API (shadow-only). Requesting review from @sophie.kim and @liam. Pending perf tests on dedicated infra.

2026-03-10: Began closed canary on k8s dev cluster with two internal services. Observed rollback_rate ~2.8% initially; investigating kernel_mismatch spikes tied to long attention patterns. Added attention-pattern flag to fingerprints.
